# Strict Lorentz improvement from an asymmetric ear at a tight triangle

This is an actual ordinary planar polygon theorem. It does not prove the generalized Lorentz inequality for arbitrary quadrilaterals, does not preserve prescribed sector areas, and makes no mixed-fiber or OC assertion.

## 1. Complete parametrization of a tight triangle

Use the balanced normals v1=(1,0), v2=(0,1), v3=(-1,-1), and source zero. For a body K write k=|K|, Qi=|K intersect {vi.x>=0}|, and sigma_i=H1(K intersect {vi.x=0})/||vi||. Set

    M=sum_i Qi/sigma_i,
    Fi=2 sqrt(k Qi)/(sigma_i M),
    Phi_i=Fi+(Fj+Fk)^2/4.

The actual-triangle theorem proves Phi_i<=2 when each cut captures a different strict vertex. Its equality characterization gives all triangles with Phi_1=2 the following form, after possibly exchanging normals 2 and 3:

    P1=(2v+w,-v-w),
    P2=(-x,x+s),
    P3=(-x,-s-w),                    x,s,v>0, w>=0.       (1)

For completeness, write an arbitrary such triangle as P1=(p,-r), P2=(-x,b), P3=(-x,-e). Equality in the first signed-row condition forces the equal first coordinates of P2,P3. The second signed-row equality is e+p+x-b-2r=0. Put v=p-r>0 and s=b-x>0. Then e-s=r-v=w. Exchanging normals 2 and 3 changes the sign of w, so one can assume w>=0 and obtain (1). These are all the strict incidence constraints. The source is interior: the barycentric coefficient of P1 is x/(p+x), while the other two numerators are xr+ep>0 and bp-xr=xv+sp>0.

Write

    b=x+s, c=x+s+w, e=s+w,
    L=x+w+2v, H=x+s+w+v, B=x+2s+w.

Thus L+B=2H, and B is the length of the vertical edge P2P3. The exact triangle data are

    k=LB/2,
    Q1=(2v+w)^2 B/(2L), sigma1=(2v+w)B/L,
    Q2=Lb^2/(2H),      sigma2=Lb/H,
    Q3=Lc^2/(2H),      sigma3=Lc/H.                    (2)

Consequently M=H, F1=L/H and F2=F3=sqrt(B/H), so Phi_1=2.

## 2. Actual asymmetric ear and exact first derivatives

Fix any t in [0,x]. For sufficiently small delta>0 set

    Q_delta=(-x-delta,t),
    K_delta=conv(P1,P2,Q_delta,P3).                    (3)

At delta=0 the new point is strictly inside the edge P2P3, even for t=0 or t=x. Thus for all sufficiently small positive delta the displayed points are cyclic vertices of a convex quadrilateral. It contains the original triangle, so zero remains interior. The new tip belongs to the closed double-signature sector opposite cap 1. No reflection symmetry of the ear is assumed.

The added triangle has area delta B/2. The original cap 1 and its chord are unchanged. Exact clipping in the added triangle gives

    k_delta=k+delta B/2,
    Q2_delta=Q2+delta[B-e^2/(e+t)]/2,
    sigma2_delta=sigma2+delta e/(e+t),
    Q3_delta=Q3+delta[B-s^2/(b+delta-t)]/2,
    sigma3_delta=sigma3+delta s/(b+delta-t).             (4)

For example, the removed negative triangle in cap 2 has fractional area e^2/[B(e+t)], and its chord contribution is delta e/(e+t). The cap-3 formula uses the actual moving height x+delta-t; it has not been replaced by its value at delta zero.

Let a prime mean the right derivative at zero. From (4),

    M'=BH/(2L) [ t/(b(e+t))+(x-t)/(c(b-t)) ].           (5)

Since F2=F3 at zero, direct differentiation gives the entirely rational identity

    Phi1'=(4-L/H)[1/(2L)-M'/H]
      +B/(2L) [ (Bt-be)/(b^2(e+t))
                  +(B(x-t)-cs)/(c^2(b-t)) ].           (6)

All denominators are positive, including at t=0,x.

## 3. Exact strictly negative derivative certificate

Put u=t/x in [0,1] and

    D=2(s+x)^2(s-t+x)(s+t+w)(s+w+x)^2(2v+w+x)(s+v+w+x).

Define the following polynomials, all with positive coefficients:

    P0=2s^2v+s^2w+s^2x+2svw+2svx+2sw^2+4swx+2sx^2
       +vw^2+2vwx+vx^2+w^3+3w^2x+3wx^2+x^3;

    P1=4s^4v+2s^4w+2s^4x+8s^3vw+4s^3vx+6s^3w^2
       +6s^3wx+8s^3x^2+6s^2vw^2+6s^2vwx+6s^2w^3
       +7s^2w^2x+12s^2wx^2+11s^2x^3+2svw^3+2svw^2x
       +2sw^4+3sw^3x+6sw^2x^2+11swx^3+6sx^4
       +w^3x^2+3w^2x^3+3wx^4+x^5;

    P2=2s^2v+s^2w+s^2x+2svw+2svx+2sw^2+2sx^2
       +vw^2+vx^2+w^3+x^3.

Set

    C0=(s+w)^2(s+x)^2 P0,
    C1=(s+x)(s+w+x) P1/2,
    C2=s^2(s+w+x)^2 P2.

Clearing the positive denominators in (5)–(6) and collecting powers of t gives the exact identity

    -D Phi1'=C0(1-u)^2+2C1 u(1-u)+C2 u^2.             (7)

Every Cj is strictly positive for x,s,v>0,w>=0. The three Bernstein basis terms are nonnegative and sum to one. Hence Phi1'<0 for every t in [0,x]. This is a polynomial identity and sign proof, not a numerical optimizer or a sampled geometric assertion.

**Theorem.** At every strict-incidence triangle saturating its first Lorentz inequality, every ear deformation (3) with tip based on the opposite double-signature part of its edge makes that inequality strict for all sufficiently small positive delta. In fact all three Lorentz inequalities are then strict.

The first assertion follows from Phi1(0)=2 and (7). To prove the second, put r=F1 and z=F2=F3 at delta zero. Then r+z^2=2 and

    4[2-z-(r+z)^2/4]=(4-z^2)(z-1)^2.

If z!=1, the other two inequalities are already strict and remain so by continuity. If z=1, all three Fi equal one. The derivative of every Phi_i is then the same sum F1'+F2'+F3', which equals the strictly negative Phi1' just proved. Thus all three become strict also in this case. All quantities in (4) are smooth for small delta>=0, so these derivative and continuity conclusions concern actual polygons.

The result is local in ear size. It does not assert monotonicity for a finite large ear, nor address triangles initially strict in every row, nor replace the missing general-body inequality.
